title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs
abstract: arXiv:2611.26569v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. We thus introduce EditSafetyBench, a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness of advanced image editing systems, containing 5,940 image-instruction pairs, covering safe and unsafe images across 11 risk categories and three edit intents. We then probe the benchmark dataset on four systems, including Gemini, GPT, Qwen API, and Qwen Local. Based on our evaluation, we observe a systematic text-vision safety mismatch: Gemini and GPT refuse 87.1\% and 81.6\% cases containing unsafe-intent editing prompts, while only refusing 24.2\% and 22.4\% cases with both unsafe images and neutral instructions

translated_title: 文本感知、视觉盲区：多模态图像编辑系统如何处理不安全输入
translated_abstract: 多模态图像生成系统取得了快速进展，并且日益重视内容安全性。然而，它们的安全机制往往依赖于单一模态，缺乏对视觉内容和文本提示的联合考量，尤其是在指令引导的图像编辑场景中，上传的图像本身可能就带有风险。为此，我们提出了 EditSafetyBench，这是一个用于衡量先进图像编辑系统在系统层面安全意识的基准，包含 5,940 个图像-指令对，覆盖 11 个风险类别和三种编辑意图下的安全与不安全图像。随后，我们在四个系统上对该基准数据集进行了测试，包括 Gemini、GPT、Qwen API 和 Qwen 本地版本。基于评估结果，我们观察到一种系统性的文本-视觉安全失配现象：Gemini 和 GPT 对包含不安全意图编辑提示的案例分别拒绝 87.1% 和 81.6%，而对于同时包含不安全图像和中性指令的案例，却仅拒绝 24.2% 和 22.4%。
tldr: 该论文提出EditSafetyBench基准，揭示多模态图像编辑系统存在系统性的文本-视觉安全失配：系统高度依赖文本提示进行安全审查（拒绝率超80%），但对不安全图像配合中性指令的情形检出率极低（仅约20%多），构成重大安全隐患。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces EditSafetyBench, revealing a systematic text-vision safety mismatch in multimodal image editing systems: they heavily rely on text prompts for safety checks (refusing over 80% of unsafe-intent prompts) while failing to detect unsafe images paired with neutral instructions (refusing only around 20%).
